title: Natural Language Processing: from text to reliable language systems
summary: 24 lessons in natural language processing, from text representation and linguistic structure to classical models, neural methods and careful evaluation. Continue into LLM mechanisms and subject assistants when ready.

lessons.title: Language as data and the unit of analysis
lessons.outcome: Treat a text dataset as records with identities, labels and families: validate the records, count documents, labels and tokens separately, and state which unit an evaluation score describes.
lessons.lab: Validate four authored support-ticket records, reject a repeated ID and blank text, count documents, classes and whitespace pieces, then audit and repair a family split.
lessons.verification: The original four rows pass and a second row with ID a raises ValueError; the fixture has 4 documents, two labels of each class and 9 pieces; unweighted accuracy stays 0.5 when the length weights are exchanged while weighted accuracy changes; the overlap {'account-reset'} disappears once a and c share a partition.

lessons.title: Unicode, normalization and loss of information
lessons.outcome: Distinguish code points, UTF-8 bytes and user-visible text, choose NFC, NFD, NFKC or case folding for a stated purpose, and keep raw spans so normalization never erases provenance.
lessons.lab: Compare two spellings of café, group compatibility characters under NFKC, case-fold Straße, decode a corrupt byte string strictly and with replacement, and store a raw span beside its NFC form.
lessons.verification: The raw spellings differ with code-point lengths (4, 5) and become equal under NFC; NFKC forms exactly two groups of two; Straße case-folds to strasse; strict decoding fails at byte 3 while replacement decoding ends with U+FFFD; the raw [0, 5) slice still reproduces the annotation.

lessons.title: Regular expressions and explainable extraction
lessons.outcome: Write regular expressions that return each match with its exact span, choose between search, match and fullmatch, separate syntactic matching from semantic validity, and score an extractor against gold entities.
lessons.lab: Extract invoice references and their spans from authored messages, reject misleading digit forms, add case alternatives that exclude 0000, and score an imperfect extractor.
lessons.verification: The two references are returned with spans (4, 12) and (26, 34); five-digit, prefixed, underscore-prefixed and non-ASCII-digit forms do not match; only inv-7777 survives the semantic rule; TP 2, FP 1 and FN 1 give precision and recall 2/3.

lessons.title: Segmentation, tokenization and subwords
lessons.outcome: Compare whitespace, punctuation-aware and subword segmentation, train byte-pair-encoding merges with a deterministic tie rule, and freeze the tokenizer so inference never changes it.
lessons.lab: Segment "can't pay." under three policies, count weighted symbol pairs for {'low': 3, 'lower': 1}, learn two merges, then encode lower, row and slow.
lessons.verification: pay sits at [6, 9); ('l', 'o') and ('o', 'w') both count 4 and ('w', '</w>') counts 3; the learned merges are ('l', 'o') then ('lo', 'w'); lower and row round-trip while slow raises an error under the restricted alphabet.

lessons.title: Morphology, syntax and linguistic structure
lessons.outcome: Keep part-of-speech context in lemmatization, trace a context rule and record its failure, and validate dependency head arrays while separating structural validity from the intended reading.
lessons.lab: Lemmatize saw, studies and better with explicit POS mappings, apply a determiner rule to saw, and check one-root, range and cycle constraints on head arrays for I saw her.
lessons.verification: saw/VERB maps to see and saw/NOUN to saw; the rule labels the old saw as VERB and the error is recorded; [1, -1, 1] is accepted while [1, 0, -1], [-1, -1], [2, -1] and empty input are rejected; [1, -1, 0] is valid but is not the intended reading.

lessons.title: N-gram models, smoothing and perplexity
lessons.outcome: Fit an add-one smoothed bigram model with BOS, EOS and UNK, derive P(we like tea) = 0.01 and perplexity sqrt(10) by hand, and explain why perplexities from different tokenizers are not comparable.
lessons.lab: Train on 'we like tea', 'we like coffee' and 'they like tea'; score 'we like tea', 'we like cocoa' and empty input.
lessons.verification: Joint probability 0.01 and perplexity 3.1623 for 'we like tea'; model state unchanged after scoring 'we like cocoa'; empty input perplexity 10.

lessons.title: Counts, TF-IDF and sparse representations
lessons.outcome: Compute document frequency, smoothed IDF and L2-normalized TF-IDF rows by hand, match scikit-learn's TfidfVectorizer, and score sparse cosine retrieval without refitting on queries.
lessons.lab: Fit TF-IDF on 'tea tea cup' and 'coffee cup', score the query tea, then transform the unseen word matcha and empty text.
lessons.verification: Document frequencies are [1, 2, 1] for [coffee, cup, tea] and IDF is [a, 1, a] with a = log(3/2) + 1; tea scores 2a/sqrt(1 + 4a^2) against the first document and 0 against the second; matcha and empty text produce no nonzero entries and leave the vocabulary unchanged.

lessons.title: Naive Bayes as a text baseline
lessons.outcome: Fit multinomial naive Bayes by hand with Laplace smoothing, compute stable log-space posteriors, match scikit-learn, and show how priors and missing negation context change the decision.
lessons.lab: Aggregate class-by-feature counts for a two-term vocabulary, smooth with alpha = 1, score the probe [1, 0] with logsumexp and compare MultinomialNB.
lessons.verification: Counts [[0, 3], [3, 1]] give likelihoods [[1/5, 4/5], [4/6, 2/6]]; the probe [1, 0] has posterior [3/13, 10/13] and MultinomialNB agrees; an all-zero probe returns the prior; urgent and not urgent receive identical posteriors under the fixed vocabulary.

lessons.title: Linear text classification and calibrated scores
lessons.outcome: Trace a logistic text classifier from features to log odds and probability, compare regularization strengths, separate the decision threshold from the model, and evaluate probabilities with the Brier score.
lessons.lab: Evaluate a two-feature logit by hand, fit a six-message classifier with a frozen vocabulary, compare C = 0.1 with C = 10, and apply thresholds 0.5 and 0.3.
lessons.verification: Logit 2.5 gives probability about 0.92414 and logits of +/-1000 stay finite; the vocabulary has six terms; the C = 0.1 coefficient norm is smaller; the thresholds give [False, False, True] and [False, True, True]; Brier scores are 0.41 and 0.26 and a probability of 1.2 raises ValueError.

lessons.title: Sequence labeling and Viterbi decoding
lessons.outcome: Decode the most probable label sequence with Viterbi in log space, check it against exhaustive enumeration, handle boundary cases, and validate BIO tag structure.
lessons.lab: Decode two-token fixtures with backpointers, enumerate all four paths as an oracle, test empty, impossible and tied inputs, and validate three BIO sequences.
lessons.verification: Initial scores are [0.36, 0.04]; the first fixture decodes to path [0, 1] with probability 0.0756 and the persistent fixture to V, V at 0.1386; empty input has log score 0, an impossible row raises ValueError and ties choose [0, 0]; token accuracy 2/3 recovers no exact ORG entity.

lessons.title: Entities, relations and extraction boundaries
lessons.outcome: Extract entity mentions with exact character spans, resolve overlapping matches, score entity-level precision, recall and F1, and extract directed relations that abstain on negation, rumor and unresolved coreference.
lessons.lab: Match a three-entity sentence with a dictionary, handle Acme versus Acme Labs and a repeated name, score predicted against gold mentions, and extract acquisition relations.
lessons.verification: Spans [0, 3), [11, 20) and [24, 29) carry PER, ORG and LOC; the longer organization wins; TP 1, FP 1 and FN 2 give precision 0.5, recall 1/3 and F1 0.4; reversed company order reverses the roles and negated or rumored sentences abstain.

lessons.title: Distributional embeddings and similarity
lessons.outcome: Build count-based word vectors from windowed co-occurrence, transform them with positive PMI, compare words by cosine similarity, and explain what rank reduction and rotation do and do not change.
lessons.lab: Count radius-one contexts for 'cat pet cat' without crossing document boundaries, compute PPMI for a 3-by-3 table, compare rows by cosine and compress to rank two.
lessons.verification: The window counts are [[0, 2], [2, 0]] and separate documents add no pairs; the first PPMI cell is log(80/49) and every value is finite and nonnegative; a zero vector gives cosine None; a shared rotation leaves cosine unchanged.

lessons.title: Topic discovery and latent structure
lessons.outcome: Fit LSA, NMF and LDA to the same small corpus, interpret each component through its words and documents, and align topic identities that a refit can permute.
lessons.lab: Fit a count vocabulary on four authored documents, then two-component TruncatedSVD, NMF and LDA, and align H with its reversed row order.
lessons.verification: The held-out word newplanet adds no column; SVD document coordinates have shape (4, 2) with reconstruction error below the zero-matrix baseline; NMF factors are nonnegative and separate pet from wheel; each LDA row sums to 1; alignment finds permutation [1, 0] with similarities [1, 1].

lessons.title: Sentence representations and semantic search
lessons.outcome: Pool token vectors into sentence vectors with padding masks, normalize them for cosine search, show what mean pooling loses, and compute an in-batch contrastive loss.
lessons.lab: Mean-pool a three-row fixture with two valid positions, compare car and automobile repair sentences, test dog bites person against person bites dog, and compute the contrastive loss at temperatures 1 and 0.5.
lessons.verification: The masked mean is [2, 3] and all-padding input raises ValueError; normalized vectors have unit norm and the synonym pair outranks dog/pet; both word orders pool to the same vector; scores [[3, 1], [1, 3]] give loss log(1 + exp(-2)), about 0.126928, which falls at temperature 0.5.

lessons.title: Contextual encoders for classification and tagging
lessons.outcome: Compute self-attention outputs that make a token depend on its neighbors, keep padding from influencing valid positions, and train document and token heads with masked supervision.
lessons.lab: Run scaled dot-product attention over the two bank contexts, append a padding vector, fit a small logistic document head and compute tagging loss with ignored labels.
lessons.verification: Bank's second output coordinate changes sign between river and money; valid outputs are unchanged by padding, whose key weights are 0; the document head's loss falls from log 2 to below 0.1 with predictions [0, 1, 0, 1]; tagging loss is log(1 + exp(-2)) and all-padding or all-ignored inputs raise ValueError.

lessons.title: Sequence-to-sequence learning and summarization
lessons.outcome: Build teacher-forced decoder inputs and targets, compute masked cross-attention, compare greedy and beam search, and keep extractive provenance for grounded summaries.
lessons.lab: Shift the target [repair], compute one-query cross-attention with and without source padding, and run width-one and width-two search on an authored probability table.
lessons.verification: [repair] becomes inputs [BOS, repair] and targets [repair, EOS]; masking the second source gives output exactly [10, 0] and an all-invalid source raises; greedy search ends at tea, EOS with probability 0.3 while the width-two beam finds coffee, EOS at 0.4; the unsupported refund query returns None.

lessons.title: Evaluating generated language without a single perfect answer
lessons.outcome: Compute clipped n-gram precision, the brevity penalty and LCS-based ROUGE-L by hand, and keep semantic failures visible beside overlap scores.
lessons.lab: Score a repeated-word candidate, 'the cat' against 'the cat sat' and the readiness minimal pair, then aggregate outcomes by family.
lessons.verification: Clipped unigram precision is 0.25, not 1; the truncated candidate scores exp(-0.5); the minimal pair has LCS 3, precision 1, recall 0.75 and F1 6/7 yet is labelled a contradiction; family rates [0.5, 0] give an equal-family mean of 0.25.

lessons.title: Multilingual NLP and domain shift
lessons.outcome: Count code points, bytes and segments across scripts, keep ambiguous language identification as an abstention, trace lossy normalization, and report language slices beside pooled metrics.
lessons.lab: Measure a Chinese string, run a narrow language-cue rule, strip marks from résumé, case-fold İ and Straße, and compute per-language accuracy.
lessons.verification: The Chinese string has 4 code points, 12 UTF-8 bytes and 1 whitespace segment; the cue rule returns en, es, None, None; résumé and resume collide after mark removal; English 0.9 and Spanish 0.5 on counts 10 and 2 give pooled accuracy 5/6 and macro accuracy 0.7.

lessons.title: Annotation, agreement and uncertain labels
lessons.outcome: Compute raw agreement and Cohen's kappa from a confusion table, show how prevalence lowers kappa, and keep adjudicated labels separate from original ratings.
lessons.lab: Write a binary urgency rubric, compute agreement and kappa for six paired labels and a 100-item prevalence case, then record soft labels and an adjudicated final label.
lessons.verification: kappa 1/3 for the six-item fixture; raw agreement 0.98 with kappa about -0.0101 for the 99/100 prevalence case; soft labels [2/3, 1, 0].

lessons.title: Weak supervision and active learning
lessons.outcome: Aggregate weak labeling functions with abstentions, diagnose coverage, conflict and correlated sources, and select active-learning examples by uncertainty under a family budget.
lessons.lab: Compute coverage and conflict for a four-row weak-label matrix, vote with ties, collapse duplicated sources, and select two uncertain examples with at most one per family.
lessons.verification: Coverage is 0.75 and conflict 0.25 overall and 1/3 among covered rows; voting gives [1, 0, -1, -1]; collapsing duplicated sources turns a majority 1 into an abstention; entropy ranks indices [0, 1] first; the family-limited selection is [0, 3] and budget 0 returns an empty batch.

lessons.title: Text leakage, duplicates and evaluation design
lessons.outcome: Detect exact and near duplicates after a declared normalization, build time- and family-aware splits, and estimate uncertainty with a family-level bootstrap.
lessons.lab: Hash two normalized router messages, compute token-set Jaccard for ready versus not ready, apply a time cutoff with family exclusion, and bootstrap paired family differences.
lessons.verification: The normalized hashes match while the raw strings stay unchanged; ready and not ready have Jaccard 0.75 despite contradicting each other; cutoff 2 gives train [a1, a2, b1], test [c1] and excluded [b2]; the equal-family mean 2/15 differs from the row-weighted 0.2; the seeded bootstrap repeats exactly.

lessons.title: Retrieval pipelines and ranking evaluation
lessons.outcome: Build an inverted index, compute BM25 scores by hand, fuse rankings with reciprocal rank fusion, and evaluate rankings with MRR and nDCG.
lessons.lab: Index three documents, score 'router reset' with BM25, fuse two supplied rankings with k = 60 and evaluate the ranking [d2, d0, d1].
lessons.verification: router has postings {d0, d1}; BM25 orders d0 > d1 > d2 = 0 and an unseen query scores all zeros; fusion puts b first with score 1/62 + 1/61 and rejects duplicate IDs; MRR is 0.5 and nDCG is (7/log2(3) + 3/2)/(7 + 3/log2(3)); restricting the corpus to d0 returns only d0.

lessons.title: Reliable NLP systems and changing corpora
lessons.outcome: Filter a changing corpus by permission and freshness, fingerprint content reproducibly, measure drift with total variation, and evaluate only mature labels.
lessons.lab: Apply a role and time rule to three source records at time 10, hash canonical records, compute total variation between [50, 50] and [80, 20], and score predictions against partly missing labels.
lessons.verification: Only policy version 2 is returned for ops, while an unknown role or time 30 returns nothing; reordering leaves the hash unchanged and a text edit changes it; the drift distance is 0.3 and invalid count vectors are rejected; two mature labels give accuracy 1 and an all-unknown batch reports count 0 with no accuracy.

lessons.title: An end-to-end domain text analytics case study
lessons.outcome: Combine identifier extraction, a frozen text classifier and permission-aware retrieval into one reviewable support-ticket analysis whose failure paths are as explicit as its normal path.
lessons.lab: Audit family separation, extract TKT identifiers, train the classifier and test held-out and out-of-vocabulary probes, then retrieve current permitted evidence for ops at time 10.
lessons.verification: No family is shared between training and held-out data; TKT-301 is canonicalized and three malformed identifiers raise ValueError; the all-OOV message is reported as unsupported vocabulary; the network case returns version 2 with the unchanged approval-rule quote, while the billing role, time 30 and malformed IDs produce insufficient-evidence results or parser failures.
